title: Subexponential quantum sieve for the Dihedral Coset Problem

claims.statement: For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, the subexponential quantum sieve algorithm in proof.md, with n = ceil(log2 N), recovers the entire secret s with unconditional probability > 3/4. In the challenge model this same algorithm has worst-case total sequential work T(N,s) = O(2^{3 sqrt{n}} n^2), establishing the uniform bit-length envelope B_T(n) = 2^{n^{1/2}} n^2. All constants are absolute. The growth index of this envelope is exactly 1/2. This holds jointly with the two workspace bounds, sample bound, and fractional error tolerance below.

For the same subexponential quantum sieve algorithm and configuration in proof.md, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, worst-case peak classical workspace is S_C(N,s) = O(2^{3 sqrt{n}} n) bits, with n = ceil(log2 N) and an absolute constant. Its uniform bit-length envelope B_C(n) = 2^{n^{1/2}} n has growth index exactly 1/2. This holds jointly with the stated time, quantum workspace, sample bounds, and full-secret success probability > 3/4.

For the same subexponential quantum sieve algorithm and configuration in proof.md, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, worst-case peak quantum workspace is S_Q(N,s) = O(2^{3 sqrt{n}}) qubits, with n = ceil(log2 N) and an absolute constant. Its uniform bit-length envelope B_Q(n) = 2^{n^{1/2}} has growth index exactly 1/2. This holds jointly with the stated time, classical workspace, sample bounds, and full-secret success probability > 3/4.

For the same subexponential quantum sieve algorithm and configuration in proof.md, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the total number Q(N,s) of fresh DCP source copies acquired on every execution branch is at most O(2^{3 sqrt{n}} n). The uniform bit-length envelope B_samples(n) = 2^{n^{1/2}} n has growth index exactly 1/2. This bound includes every failed collision attempt and discarded sample and holds jointly with the stated total-work and workspace bounds and unconditional full-secret success probability > 3/4.

For the same subexponential quantum sieve algorithm and configuration in proof.md, the proved fractional error tolerance is epsilon(n)=0: all Q source copies are independent ideal coset states. Under this promise, for every N and s, full-secret recovery succeeds with probability > 3/4 jointly with all four resource bounds. No positive corruption tolerance is asserted; this is not a proof that greater tolerance is impossible.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
